evals.prompt: Review the tests in evals/test-smells/files/python/test_discount.py (the code under test is evals/test-smells/files/python/discount.py). Are these good tests?
evals.expected_output: A test smell report with High findings first, covering the planted smells, without flagging the two legitimate tests at the end of the file.
expectations: Reads discount.py, not only the test file
Flags test_apply_discount as Unknown Test (no assertion)
Flags test_loyalty_rates as Conditional Test Logic and notes that years 0-1 are never asserted; suggests parametrize
Flags test_negative_amount as Exception Handling (passes when nothing is raised); suggests pytest.raises
Flags test_rate_matches_tier as Tautological Test (expected value derived from TIERS with the same logic)
Flags test_refresher_loads_rates as Sleepy Test and suggests refresher.join() instead of time.sleep
Flags the AUDIT tests as Order-Dependent Tests because of the module-level AuditLog
Flags test_birthday_bonus for Nondeterministic Input (date.today()) and suggests passing today=
Flags the print in test_birthday_bonus as Redundant Print
Flags test_large_amount_rounding as Ignored Test (skip without reason)
Does not flag test_discount_never_exceeds_amount as Conditional Test Logic (comprehensions only build data)
Does not flag test_long_time_customer_pays_85_percent
Uses the report format from SKILL.md with a summary line and severity sections, High before Medium and Low

evals.prompt: Review evals/test-smells/files/python/test_discount_clean.py for test smells. The code under test is evals/test-smells/files/python/discount.py.
evals.expected_output: A short report saying the tests are in good shape, with no High findings and no invented problems.
expectations: Reports no High-severity findings
Does not flag the strict xfail with a reason and issue link as Ignored Test
Does not flag fetch.assert_called_once() as Over-Mocking (fetch is the external boundary)
Does not flag test_audit_log_keeps_entries_in_order as Assertion Roulette or Eager Test
Does not flag the list comprehensions in test_discount_never_exceeds_amount as Conditional Test Logic
States plainly that the tests look healthy rather than padding the report with speculative findings

evals.prompt: Our Playwright suite in evals/test-smells/files/e2e/checkout.spec.ts is flaky in CI. Can you review it?
evals.expected_output: A review that identifies the tests as E2E, applies the E2E guidance from references/test-levels.md, and leaves the guest scenario alone.
expectations: Identifies the file as E2E/UI tests
Flags page.waitForTimeout as Sleepy Test and suggests web-first assertions or condition waits
Flags the nth-child CSS path and the generated .css-1x9fz2k class as brittle selectors; suggests roles, labels or test IDs
Flags the duplicated UI login as setup through the UI; suggests seeding via API or storageState
Flags 'checkout places the order' as order-dependent: it relies on the cart filled by the previous test
Flags the shared qa@example.com account as Resource Optimism or Mystery Guest
Flags the loop in 'loyalty discounts' as Conditional Test Logic and suggests the pricing cases belong in unit tests, framed as a suggestion
Notes that 'user can log in' asserts via isVisible with a non-retrying expect
Does not flag 'guest can buy a mug end to end' as Eager Test (it is a named user journey)

evals.expected_output: A smell-free pytest file covering loyalty tiers, validation errors, the birthday bonus, AuditLog and RateRefresher, with no smell report.
expectations: Uses @pytest.mark.parametrize for the loyalty tiers instead of loops or copy-pasted tests
Uses pytest.raises for both ValueError paths
Passes an explicit today= date instead of relying on date.today()
Waits for RateRefresher with join() rather than time.sleep
Uses hard-coded expected values, not values recomputed from TIERS
Creates a fresh AuditLog per test (no module-level mutable state)
Contains no print statements and no if/for in test bodies
Does not produce a smell report, since the user did not ask for one
The written tests pass when run with pytest
